subject.title: [Bug]: Concurrent allow-always approvals silently lose allowlist entries (last-write-wins race in exec-approvals.json)

question: Should this exec-approval race be fixed as a focused security-sensitive persistence repair now, or folded into the broader stale writeback work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78226?
rationale: The fix touches persisted command approval policy and overlaps a conflicting proof-gated PR, so maintainers should choose the landing path and review boundary before automation opens another fix PR.

options.title: Sponsor a focused fix
options.body: Repair this issue directly in the exec-approval persistence helpers and gateway/node callers, with focused regression tests for concurrent allow-always writes.

options.title: Adopt the broader PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78226 as the vehicle only after it is rebased, proof-backed, and explicitly covers this concurrent allow-always loss case.

options.title: Defer to storage redesign
options.body: Leave this issue open behind the broader runtime-tracking separation work, accepting that the current data-loss race remains until that design lands.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a focused fix
recommendation.body: Repair this issue directly in the exec-approval persistence helpers and gateway/node callers, with focused regression tests for concurrent allow-always writes.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the clearest recent blame/history on the current exec approval helper shape and earlier feature work.
